gpt.text:
Run the three commands in the order shown; they’re already sequenced sensibly for (1) module-level exploration, then (2) system-level candidate runs, then (3) generating the next targeted fix report.

## 1) Module autopilot (select best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
**What it does:** runs the module registry experiments and updates selection to the best-performing module set (based on your configured metrics), producing run artifacts/logs.

**After it finishes, check:**
- The “selected best” summary in stdout/logs
- Any updated champion/best pointers in your baseline outputs (depends on how your tool writes results)

## 2) System autopilot (full system candidates)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
**What it does:** evaluates end-to-end system candidates defined in `system_candidates.yaml`.

**After it finishes, check:**
- Which candidates are PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE
- Whether any candidate beats the current champion’s key stats (tuning + lockbox means/mins)

## 3) Generate next fix report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
**What it does:** produces a targeted “next fix” markdown report based on the latest experiment outcomes, aimed at resolving the most likely blockers/regressions.

---

## If you want a quick sanity checklist before/after
- Confirm the current champion file exists: `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json`
- Capture logs for later diffing (optional): pipe stdout/stderr to a timestamped file for each run
- After all three, open: `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` and follow the top recommendation first

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the resulting PASS/FAIL tables), I can help interpret whether anything actually surpasses the current champion and what to try next.
